title: Plain-text angle brackets are treated as HTML markup

evidence.quote:
/// Processed content (HTML or Markdown)
    public let content: String

DigestArticle(
            title: title,
            author: author,
            content: content,

reasoning: The domain allows article content to be HTML or Markdown, but the UI uses tag-stripping regexes and wraps plain text into HTML without escaping raw '<' and '>' characters. Markdown/plain text such as 'List<String>', '2 < 3', or quoted XML can be stripped or misparsed in previews and the reader, corrupting the article text in the core reading flow.
reproduction: Create a processed article whose content is Markdown/plain text containing 'List<String>' or '2 < 3 and x > y', then view it in DigestDetailView/EinkReaderView; the preview or rendered reader text can drop or reinterpret the bracketed content.
recommendation: Separate trusted HTML from plain Markdown/text before rendering. For plain text, escape &, <, and > before adding generated tags, or build an AttributedString directly from text/Markdown instead of regex-based HTML wrapping. Avoid regex tag stripping for user-visible previews unless the content is known HTML.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included unit test is a placeholder and the screenshot test only validates navigation with fixture content; neither asserts content fidelity for Markdown/plain-text articles with angle brackets.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a reader formatting test that renders an article containing 'List<String>' and '2 < 3' and asserts those exact strings are present in the preview and paginated reader text.
minimumFixScope: ArticleCard.plainTextPreview and TextPaginator.buildArticleBody content escaping/parsing logic.
